//: Story Phase 4, chapter 19: The Worst Forecast Yet. Late afternoon of day 7. Three repairs on the port rail (board at (16,19), rope brace at (16,21), weak section at (16,23)), each faced from x=15. Garrick walks the deck with his tray-clipboard. The worst forecast, the Center coming back, an evacuation aft (or forward; either band of the deck), the fresh repair eaten, the forecast drunk, three hundred more, the yellow wake, and tomorrow's forecast. Story Phase 4 ends there.

p4c5.begin.narrate: The Dead Center finally slid off the port rail and wandered away aft, looking pleased with itself. The sharks calmed down. Somewhat.

p4c5.repairs: The port rail looks like a biscuit someone has been nibbling round the edges of.
jory[determined]: Aye, Captain! Three jobs on the port rail, and I need hands on all of them. A board where the rail was, a rope brace, and a patch on the weak section.

p4c5.repairs.tutorial: Help with the repairs: three jobs on the port rail (right-hand side). Stand at the rail beside each one, face it and press Confirm.
p4c5.repairs.title: Repair It Again

p4c5.fix_board: A gap in the rail as wide as a man. Jory has left a new board and a bag of nails beside it.
It's not pretty. It's a board. It'll keep a man from falling in, and that's what a rail is for.
p4c5.fix_rope: The rail stanchion here is chewed half through. It needs a rope brace, hauled tight to the next one.
Tight as a drum. It hums when the wind blows. Nobody likes the sound it makes.
p4c5.fix_patch: A soft section of hull, just above the waterline, where the planks have been bitten thin.
Good oak over bad oak. Jory chalks something on it. You don't ask what.

then: jory[happy]: That's the lot, Captain! Rail, brace, patch. She's whole again. Near enough.
The crew stand back and look at their work. For the first time in a week, somebody smiles.

then.tutorial: Garrick has a new forecast. Check it (talk to him).
then.title: Repair It Again

p4c5.supervisor: The Grand Stenchmaster is strolling along the deck with a galley tray under his arm, with a sheet of paper pinned to it and a crayon tucked behind his ear.
garrick[proud]: Excellent work, everyone! Excellent! Keep it up!
garrick[businesslike]: Supervisors don't hammer, Mister Pete.
garrick[smug]: No. I'm the Grand Stenchmaster. And the Grand Stenchmaster outranks supervisor.
Nobody agrees. Nobody says so, either. They go back to hammering, harder than they need to.

then: mags: Fresh ration for the workers, Captain. Don't look at it.
She hands you a mug of Frog Grog. It has a bubble in it.

p4c5.worst: garrick[proud]: Fresh off the crayon, Captain.
It is worse than all the others.

There is a massive yellow blob. There are six skulls. There is a shark wearing a crown. The galley has been drawn as a sandwich. Your cabin has been drawn as a little house with stink coming out of the chimney, and it is labelled STINKBEARD HOUSE.
captain: Why is my cabin 'Stinkbeard House'?
captain[determined]: Just tell me where the Center goes next.
He licks a finger and holds it up into the wind.
garrick[alarmed]: THE CENTER IS COMING BACK.
Garrick points. At the port rail. At the new board, the new rope, the patch Jory finished five minutes ago.

p4c5.worst.tutorial: The Center is coming back for the fresh repair. Evacuate! Get clear: aft by the cabin door, or forward by the bell.
p4c5.worst.title: Repair It Again

p4c5.fresh_repair: From a safe distance, the whole crew watch the Dead Center roll up to the port rail, over the new board, down the side of the ship, and into the sea beside the fresh patch.
The new board lasts about four seconds. A shark takes it clean off the rail and swims away with it, like a dog with a stick.
Another one bites straight through the rope brace. It twangs off into the water.
jory[annoyed]: That took us an hour. That took us an HOUR.
pete[tired]: We're repairing it slower than they're eating it.
jory: ...We're repairing it slower than they're eating it.
Nobody says anything for a while. Under the comedy of it all, it has started to feel like the sort of thing that sinks ships.
garrick[businesslike]: Well. That forecast's done its job.
He crumples it into a ball, and tosses it over his shoulder.
Into your fresh Frog Grog.
You look at the drink. At Garrick. At the sharks. At the Center, wandering off. At your ship.
At Squawks.
squawks[worried]: ...Bad day?
captain[tired]: Aye.
squawks[neutral]: Squawks drink the Frog Grog?
captain[tender]: No.
garrick[businesslike]: Are you going to finish that, Captain?
You hand him the mug.
The Grand Stenchmaster drinks the forecast. Paper and all.
garrick[happy]: Waste not.
The whole crew stare at him.
He pats his stomach, and hands you back the empty mug.
captain[tired]: Do not tell me how many.
rook[alarmed]: Where are they all COMING from?
Garrick points astern.
Behind the Queen Anne's Revenge, all the way to the horizon, a long, wide, glowing yellow stripe lies on the sea. It's her wake. Every shark within a hundred miles is swimming up it.
garrick[businesslike]: They don't need word of mouth, Captain.
garrick[proud]: We've been ADVERTISING.
garrick[proud]: Which brings me to... TOMORROW'S FORECAST.
You turn, very slowly.
One giant yellow scribble, covering the entire ship. In the corner: VERY BAD.
garrick[businesslike]: Seventy percent chance of stink.
You look around. At the stained deck, the sweating ropes, the coughing bell, the bald parrot, the yellow wake, the permanent, total, all-encompassing stink.
captain[tired]: ...Seventy?
garrick[businesslike]: ...
He thinks about it.
He adds another zero.
garrick[businesslike]: Seven hundred percent.
captain[tired]: ...That seems more accurate.

p4c5.finale.narrate: And so, as the sun went down, the Queen Anne's Revenge sailed on: patched, and re-patched, and patched for the patches, trailing a yellow stripe to the edge of the world.
Her crew ate biscuits on the deck. Her bell coughed the hour. Somewhere below, the Dead Center went and lay down in the treasure room, like a dog that has had a very full day.
Behind her, several hundred fins came on at a steady pace, and a few more joined them every hour.
At her wheel stood Captain Stinkbeard, with a bald parrot inside his coat, and he did not ask where the Center would be tomorrow. He already knew.
It would be wherever it was needed least.

p4c5.coda: Tomorrow's forecast is posted on the board. It says VERY BAD. Everybody has agreed that seven hundred percent seems about right.

p4c5.coda.tutorial: Story Phase 4 is complete. The ship is yours to explore: the crew have plenty to say, the Forecast Board keeps every forecast, and Jory will let you take a Shark Duty shift if you really want one. The story continues in the next chapter.
p4c5.coda.title: To Be Continued
